Field notes · October

Autumn at the footbridge

What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

The river

The river rose twice that week, and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

MLMaya Lindqvist5m ago

Two days is optimistic. Last time the same job took a week; say so, or give a range.

The path

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Delete this comment?

It has no replies.

Nothing is left in its place.

Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To show something whole that the page only names: a long piece of text behind a "View" action, a full log, the text of a file.
  • When the person reads or copies it and comes straight back to where they were.

When not to use

  • For a few extra links or actions under a button: use cmp-popover-menu.
  • For a message about the content beside it: use cmp-inline-alert.
  • For a step in a flow, a form or a page of its own: give it its own screen.
  • To interrupt with a confirmation nobody asked for.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

Not applicable: one look. A raised panel on a dimmed page, as wide as its content allows up to the readable measure and never wider than the screen, with its header fixed and its body scrolling.

Anatomy

  • Root: <dialog class="ds-dialog" data-ds="dialog" aria-labelledby="<title id>">, the native element. data-ds lets component.js open and close it; it is modal while open (showModal()).
  • ds-dialog__header: the top bar, holding the heading, the actions and the close button.
  • ds-dialog__heading: ds-dialog__title (an <h2> with the id the root names) and, optionally, ds-dialog__meta (one short line: who it is for, its length) (with-meta).
  • ds-dialog__actions (optional, with-actions): where the page puts the dialog's few controls (a segmented control, a copy button). The dialog lays them out; their look is their own.
  • ds-dialog__close: a <button type="button" data-ds-dialog-close> with the word "Close", always last in the header.
  • ds-dialog__body: the content, which scrolls on its own while the header stays.
  • Opening: any element with data-ds-dialog-open="<dialog id>" opens it; a script may also call showModal().

Accessibility

  • A native modal <dialog>: the page behind is inert while it is open, and focus moves into it (to the first control in the header).
  • Its name is its title (aria-labelledby); the meta line is part of the header, read after the title.
  • Esc closes it, as does Close and a click on the dimmed page around it. Focus returns to the control that opened it.
  • The body scrolls with the keyboard (it is focusable when it overflows) and with the pointer; nothing is cut off.
  • Text meets AA on the raised surface in every theme; the close button meets the minimum target size.

Interaction

  • Opening fades the panel and the dimmed page in over --ds-motion-settle on --ds-motion-ease, and the panel rises by the lift distance; closing plays the same in reverse, then focus returns to the opener. While it fades out it takes no clicks. Under the still preset and reduced motion it appears and goes at once (int-04, int-06).
  • Close answers hover and press with a colour change only, and shows the shared focus ring (int-01, int-02, int-03).
  • Nothing in the page behind moves when it opens; the page does not scroll under it.

Contract

  • Parts: the scrim, a dimmed layer over the whole page behind; the panel, a raised box centred on the screen (ds-dialog); the header, a fixed bar across the panel's top (ds-dialog__header) holding the heading (the title, and an optional one-line meta below it: ds-dialog__title, ds-dialog__meta), an optional group of the page's own few controls (ds-dialog__actions), and the Close button, always last (ds-dialog__close); the body, the content below the header, which scrolls on its own (ds-dialog__body); and the opener, any control outside it that names it and opens it.
  • States: closed (nothing shows); opening (the scrim and the panel fade in, and the panel settles into place); open (modal: the page behind takes no input, focus is inside the panel, the header stays while the body scrolls, and the body can take focus only when its content overflows); closing (the scrim and the panel fade out and the panel takes no clicks; a second close while it fades finishes it at once); then closed again, with focus back on the opener. Opening one that is already open does nothing. Close has default, hover and focus.
  • Inputs: activating an opener (click, tap, or Enter or Space on it) opens it and remembers the opener. Close (click, tap, Enter or Space), Esc, and a click or tap on the scrim outside the panel all close it; a click inside the panel never closes it. Tab and Shift+Tab move among the controls inside it only; the page behind cannot be reached while it is open. When the body overflows, it takes focus in the tab order and scrolls with the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End; it also scrolls with the wheel and touch without scrolling the page behind.
  • Events: tells the screen when it has closed (the native close event, raised once it has faded out, however it was closed); while open it makes the rest of the screen unreachable, and on closing it returns focus to the control that opened it (if that control is still on the screen). A script may open and close it by name (dsDialog.open(dialog, opener), dsDialog.close(dialog)).
  • Geometry: the panel is centred both ways, as wide as the readable measure plus --ds-space-8 but never wider than the screen less --ds-space-6, and at most the screen's height less --ds-space-8 tall; its corners are --ds-radius-surface, its edge --ds-border-width, and it casts --ds-shadow-overlay. The header has --ds-space-3 above, below and on the right and --ds-space-5 on the left (--ds-space-4 on a screen 720 px wide or narrower), with --ds-space-3 between its parts, which wrap to a second line when they do not fit; the body has --ds-space-5 on every side (--ds-space-4 on a narrow screen). Close is at least --ds-target-min tall with --ds-space-3 on its sides. Opening moves the panel down along the vertical axis from twice --ds-motion-lift above its place to its place, and closing moves it back up the same distance; nothing turns. Everything eases over --ds-motion-settle and is instant under the still preset and reduced motion.
  • Looks: the scrim is the strong surface at 45% opacity; the panel is the raised surface with a hairline default-border edge and default text; the title is medium size and strong weight, the meta smaller and muted; the header has a hairline line under it; Close is a muted word with no edge, which gets a sunken fill and default text on hover and the shared focus ring on focus. See the specimen's default × default cell (shown in place, not over a dimmed page).
  • Names: the dialog is known by its id, which its opener names (aria-controls) and a script opens it by; its heading names it for assistive technology.
  • Focus: opening moves focus to the first control in the panel (Close when there is no other); focus stays inside while it is open; closing returns it to the opener, or to the page's start when the opener is gone. The panel shows at once on opening.

Content rules

  • The title names what is shown, in a few words: the same title as the card or row that opened it ("Release notes").
  • The meta line, when present, is one short line: "Version 2.4 · 3 minutes to read".
  • The close button says "Close"; no other button closes it.
  • At most two or three actions in the header, each one or two words.

Do and don't

  • Do open it from a button that names what it shows ("View release notes"), and return focus there on close.
  • Do keep the header to the title, a few actions and Close, so the body has the room.
  • Don't put a form or a multi-step flow in it.
  • Don't open one dialog from another.
